points.text: Contribution incremental: refines SWE-Bench rather than new methodology or insight.
Narrow language coverage (mainly Python, JS/TS, Go).
Small-to-mid repositories and startup codebases do not show enterprise-level or industrial realism.
Evaluation tied to single SWE-Agent scaffold; other frameworks not evaluated.
Failure analysis descriptive, lacking causal interpretation.
Human-provided requirements and interface hints undermine autonomy claim.
Long-horizon operationalized as lines changed, conflating patch size with task complexity; oversold.
Limited language coverage; Java, C++, Rust missing.
Ambiguity reduction leaves untested agent ability to handle under-specified real tasks.
Long-horizon term misleading given modest changes and 50-call budget; turn counts unreported.
Only a single agent harness evaluated.
No inference-time scaling or sampling; only pass@1.
Complexity measured by files and lines; diff-hunk distribution should be provided.
Unclear whether new tests were added after dropping broad tests.
Purchasing startup repositories as contamination prevention unconvincing; agreement details absent.
No discussion why purchasing beats continuous-evolution approaches like SWE-bench Live.
Single agent scaffold; difficulty gap may be scaffold-specific.
Only four languages versus seven or more in prior benchmarks.
GPL licensing is a legal, not technical, barrier to training-data inclusion.
No empirical contamination analysis such as memorization probes or cutoff comparisons.
Public set will be crawled and commits are historical; contamination resistance unsupported.
Held-out set never evaluated, so overfitting check not demonstrated.
Commercial set unverifiable, vendor conflicts of interest, no repository information.
Commercial tasks called more complex based only on lower resolve rates.
Commercial tasks per repository contradict stated constraint; per-repo results noisy.
Reported numbers in tables and text inconsistent.
Table 3 counts exceed N; denominators unclear.
Failure categories in table differ from judge prompt; mapping unexplained.
LLM judge validation lacks sample size or agreement figures.
Judge is also an evaluated model, risking self-preference bias.
Single label per trajectory conflates symptom and cause.
Failure interpretation confounded by scaffold and prompt incompatibility.
Single scaffold and prompt; Agentless dropped without numbers; strong scaffolds not evaluated.
Single run without confidence intervals, seeds, or temperature; differences within noise.
Few open-weight models evaluated; some model versions outdated.
Human-written requirements leak test specifics, turning task into spec-following.
False negatives from valid alternative solutions not quantified.
Effect of requirement augmentation not ablated.
Hours-to-days long-horizon claim unsupported; LOC proxy is modest.
Enterprise-level and industrial relevance claims unsubstantiated; GPL selection biases distribution.
Novelty and first claims lack comparison with prior pipelines; related work omits benchmarks.
Difficulty filtering mentioned but undescribed; possible selection against models.
SWE-Bench Verified comparison confounds several factors.
Dataset-creation details missing: annotators, agreement, stage yields.
Repository list and per-split distributions not provided.
Inconsistent wording about per-repo caps and held-out mirroring.
Cost, token usage, and turn statistics not reported.
